messages:
Sara Chen: quick heads-up — RFC incoming: we want to change the audit event payload for better forensic fidelity. proposed deltas: add `actor_ip` (string), add `sampling_rate` (float), remove `session_id` (deprecated), and standardize `event_schema_version`. need migration strategy, RBAC constraints, and customer validation plan. Thoughts?
Mike Ortega: +1 on actor_ip. question: do we need PII gating for IPs? can we store hashed IP instead? @Sara Chen
Jules Park: for incident response we prefer raw IP in internal logs. suggestion: keep raw `actor_ip` encrypted at rest, expose hashed/obfuscated version to non-security roles. RBAC: only `security-admin` and `audit-service` can decrypt.
Kyra Patel: agree on encryption. this ties into KMS rotation — are we okay with per-customer keys? that'll complicate rollouts.
Devon Lee: per-customer KMS would be ideal for compliance customers but heavy ops. alternative: key-wrapping with a root CMK + org-wrapped keys. we should surface key model in the RFC.
Sara Chen: noted. on versioning — proposal: explicit `event_schema_version` integer in every event; dual-write for a 6-week window, and runtime schema gate `audit.v2.enable` per-tenant for reads. After 6 weeks, flip default and keep v1 read-only for 90 days before pruning. thoughts on timeline?
Mike Ortega: timeline seems reasonable. for dual-write, ensure we have deterministic mapping for removed fields (session_id) so consumers can fall back. Also add a `deprecated_fields` array in v2 metadata to help clients.
Jules Park: propose this sample snippet for v2 event (internal example):
```json
{
  "event_schema_version": 2,
  "event_type": "token.create",
  "actor": { "id": "user_123", "type": "user" },
  "actor_ip": "ENC[AES256_GCM]:...",
  "actor_ip_obfuscated": "hash:abcd1234",
  "sampling_rate": 0.05,
  "payload": { "resource": "token", "result": "success" },
  "metadata": { "deprecated_fields": ["session_id"] }
}
```
Kyra Patel: love the `actor_ip_obfuscated` field for non-privileged consumers. question: do we need to add `consent_basis` for GDPR cases? might be required for EU customers when storing IPs.
Devon Lee: add `consent_basis` (string enum) optional. will need schema-level validation and a flag when we accept IPs for EU tenants. add to tenant profile.
audit-bot: automated diff: v1 -> v2 changes detected: +actor_ip, +actor_ip_obfuscated, +sampling_rate, +event_schema_version, +metadata.deprecated_fields; -session_id.
Sara Chen: good. next: customer-facing validation. plan: build a lightweight validator CLI and a console page where customers can upload sample streams and see a compatibility report (breaking fields highlighted). also provide a compatibility mode flag `accept_only_v1` during cutover.
Mike Ortega: add a webhook hook so partners can subscribe to compatibility warnings during the dual-write window. also send a one-off CSV export of impacted tenants with examples.
Jules Park: operational concerns: logging retention and cost. adding `sampling_rate` suggests we should implement adaptive telemetry to avoid explosion. for forensic cases we can full-log on flagged incidents.
Kyra Patel: security review items: update threat model for new encrypted fields (key access patterns), update RBAC docs to show who can request decryption, and add alerting if `actor_ip` decryption requests spike.
Devon Lee: vuln triage: we should run a focused SAST/DAST pass on the new deserialization path for schema v2, and expand unit tests around canonicalization of IP hashing to avoid collisions.
Sara Chen: ok action list: 1) Draft RFC (include KMS options + RBAC rules + timeline) — @Mike Ortega 2) Validator prototype + console view — @Jules Park 3) KMS/key-model writeup — @Devon Lee 4) Security review checklist & threat model update — @Kyra Patel 5) Customer comms template + webhook CSV — @Sara Chen. Please ack and estimate by EOD.
Mike Ortega: ack — will send RFC draft by tomorrow noon.
Jules Park: ack — prototyping validator this week, ETA Thu.
Kyra Patel: ack — security checklist by Fri.
Devon Lee: ack — KMS writeup by Fri as well.
audit-bot: reminder scheduled: schema-rfc-review meeting set for 2049123500 (in 8 minutes)
Sara Chen: thanks team — we'll capture blockers in the RFC. If any compliance/legal folks need to weigh in early, ping me and I'll loop them in. :thumbsup:
